scenes.script_line: Think about the last time a story changed your mind. A film that stayed with you for days. A conversation that made you see someone differently. Stories have always been one of the most powerful ways to shape how people think, feel and act. Leaders know this. Brands know this. Whole organisations invest heavily in shaping the stories people believe, because whoever shapes the story often shapes the behaviour. Stories shape perception. Perception shapes decisions. And decisions shape outcomes.

scenes.script_line: But this isn't only happening out there, in the media or in business. The most powerful stories in your life are the ones you tell about yourself. "I'm not good with money." "I always mess up relationships." "People like me don't get opportunities." These internal stories quietly decide how you read your experiences, what you believe is possible, and how you show up every day. And over time, they become familiar. They feel true, even when they're not.

scenes.script_line: Take a moment and think of one sentence you often say about yourself. Something that starts with "I'm just…" or "I always…" or "I could never…" That sentence is a story. And it has probably been running for a long time. Here's the good news. A story is not a fact. It's an interpretation, and interpretations can be questioned. When you bring awareness to the stories you tell yourself, you create the chance to question them. And when you question them, you create the possibility to change them. That's what this workshop is about.

scenes.script_line: You'll work through a ten-step process, shown on page one of your workbook. It moves in a circle, and each step builds on the one before. First, you'll get clear on what matters most to you. Then you'll name the area of your life where your story isn't working, and why it needs to change. Next comes the honest part. You'll unpack the old story in detail, acknowledge how it has served you, and see clearly why it isn't true. scenes.script_line: You won't be doing this alone. Your facilitator is here to guide you through each step, and after each short video, you'll have time to write in your workbook. There are no right or wrong answers. The more honest you are with the page, the more this process will give back to you. Three things will help you get the most from this time. First, be honest rather than impressive. Nobody will grade your workbook. Write what's real, not what sounds good. Second, write it down.
